quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of crashing?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Ride in parts of the lane where you cannot be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to tell others what you will do. Stay visible to other drivers. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle can cause serious danger more easily than in a car.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, at intersections, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should also discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose because motorcycles are small.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
Don't use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Use turn signals whenever you plan to change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby. Signals are very important for your safety as a rider.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding alongside a car?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot, and the car will block your escape path.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap.
questions.explanation: Wear jackets and sturdy pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear boots that cover and support your ankles. Wear sturdy gloves. These items protect you in a crash.

questions.question: What do you NOT need to check on your tires?
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, general wear, and tread depth.

questions.question: When does Massachusetts law require you to use your motorcycle headlight?

options.text: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
Only when driving near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise. It is safest to use your headlight whenever you ride.

questions.question: What should you do when you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat so your legs absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: Approach the object at a right angle and slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle straight. Rise slightly off your seat so your legs can absorb the shock. Just before contact, roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can reach the ground when you sit on it. You should be able to reach and operate all controls easily.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight while riding.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight and ride in a position that lets oncoming traffic see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can avoid danger if needed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may finish passing in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should use your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You must start and finish all passing moves only in areas where passing is legal and safe.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: You can improve your visibility by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright-colored or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when appropriate.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following, except:

options.text: The air pressure in the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Damage to the paint.
questions.explanation: Before getting on a motorcycle, check the tire tread and air pressure, fluid levels, and lights and signals.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you drink only one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on your body.
Your body is affected, but only for a short time.
Your body is affected, but coffee will eliminate it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect the skills you need to ride safely. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact. This reduces the force that could throw you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands properly.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like most foods and drinks. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker right away.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested, so it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. However, your body gets rid of alcohol slowly—about one drink per hour.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black letters show traffic rules, like speed limits. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding for protection. Even in warm weather, a leather jacket can help protect you and keep you cool. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to work in hot weather.

questions.question: Wearing a helmet is:

options.text: Required for both riders and passengers.
Optional for both riders and passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for both riders and passengers.
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires both motorcycle riders and passengers to wear helmets. A DOT-approved helmet is the best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: You have had alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from drinking.
You will be okay as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from drinking.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system. Even after waiting, your judgment and abilities may still be affected.
